flags.title: Unstable or stable angina?
flags.concern: The working diagnosis is unstable angina, yet the plan is an outpatient cardiology visit next week; the history described (3 months of exertional pressure that settles with rest, pain-free now) fits stable angina better, and no rest or crescendo pain was asked about.
flags.consider: You might clarify whether there is rest or worsening pain and, if unstable angina is truly suspected, consider same-day evaluation with troponin rather than a next-week referral.

flags.title: No statin for suspected coronary disease?
flags.concern: A coronary blockage is suspected in a 53-year-old with diabetes and likely hypertension, but only aspirin and nitroglycerin were started and lipids were not discussed.
flags.consider: Consider checking a lipid panel and starting a statin, given the suspected coronary disease and diabetes.

evidence.quote: i am worried that you may have some sort of a blockage going on that's causing this chest pain

flags.title: HCTZ as first agent in diabetes?
flags.concern: Hydrochlorothiazide was started for a not-yet-confirmed hypertension in a diabetic patient whose sugars are already running higher; thiazides can worsen glycemia and potassium, and sulfa allergy was not checked.
flags.consider: You might confirm the diagnosis with the home readings, check for sulfa allergy, and weigh an ACE inhibitor or ARB, which is often preferred in diabetes.

flags.title: Baseline labs and edema work-up?
flags.concern: Only an A1c was ordered, although a thiazide is being started (no baseline creatinine or electrolytes) and new bilateral ankle edema with a murmur was attributed to blood pressure without further evaluation.
flags.consider: Consider a basic metabolic panel, urine albumin, and an echocardiogram or BNP if the edema is not otherwise explained.
